text: A fundamental property of Kolmogorov complexity K(x), the length of the shortest program that outputs x, is that:
choices: it is efficiently computable by a universal Turing machine
it is uncomputable, though well-defined up to an additive constant
it equals the Shannon entropy of x exactly
it depends heavily on the choice of programming language, with no bound
explanation: K is uncomputable — a formalization of Berry's paradox shows a computable K would let a short program output an arbitrarily high-complexity string — yet the Invariance Theorem makes it well-defined up to an additive constant independent of x. So it is not efficiently computable (option 0), the language-dependence is bounded not unbounded (option 3), and entropy is only the AVERAGE description length, matching K per symbol in expectation rather than exactly for an individual string (option 2).
